# R-D: source text availability at validate time (007 T001)

**Risk traced**: research.md D8 R-D / D6 — whether a datasheet's source block text (the
`composition`/`options`/`equipment` tuples `pipeline/parse/wahapedia_html_dom.py`'s `Datacard`
carries) is still reachable in-process when `validate`'s call sites run, so the equivalence check
(007 US5) can compare against it without a new acquisition.

## Verdict: REFUTED, as originally framed — with a precise, usable alternative

The source text is **not** reachable at either of `validate`'s two current call sites. It **is**
reachable, in-process, at one specific point that is not either of those call sites: inside
`build`'s own `with workspace(root) as work:` block in `pipeline/cli.py`, before that block ends.

## What was traced

1. **`pipeline/workspace.py`'s `workspace()`** is a context manager that empties `work/` on entry
   and again in a `finally` on exit — the on-disk copy of any acquired source is gone the moment
   the `with` block is left, by any route (normal return, exception, `KeyboardInterrupt`).

2. **`pipeline/cli.py`'s build flow** (the function beginning ~line 680) opens exactly one such
   block: `with workspace(root) as work:` (line 718) through line 767. Inside it,
   `detail = read_detail(config, detail_payloads)` (line 733) is assigned — `detail` is a
   `dict[str, CsvReadResult]` (`pipeline/parse/wahapedia_csv.py::CsvReadResult`), and its
   `rows: tuple[WahapediaRow, ...]` carry the source text as row-field values, in **both**
   acquisition modes: `read_export_payloads` (csv mode) and `read_datacard_payloads` (html mode,
   `pipeline/parse/wahapedia_html_dom.py`) are both registered as `DetailReader`s returning the
   same `dict[str, CsvReadResult]` shape (`pipeline/acquire/detail_source.py`'s `READERS` table),
   so `detail` carries the datasheet's source text regardless of mode. `Datacard.composition` /
   `.options` / `.equipment` (`tuple[str, ...]`) are the html-mode reader's own intermediate
   representation of that same text before it is folded into row fields.

3. **`detail` is scoped to that block on purpose, not by accident.** The existing code comment at
   cli.py lines ~753-759 states it directly for the mechanic-digest computation, which already
   runs inside this same block for exactly this reason: *"the mechanic digest may only be
   computed while the detail source's text is in hand ... which is here and only here — `detail`
   goes out of scope with `work/` at the end of this block."* This is the established precedent
   the equivalence check (T052) should follow, not a new pattern to invent.

4. **`check_snapshot(snapshot, meta)`** — one of the two named `validate`-stage call sites — is
   invoked at cli.py line 805, **after** the `with workspace(root) as work:` block has already
   exited (dedent at line 769). At that point `detail` is out of scope and `work/` has already
   been emptied on disk. Neither `snapshot` nor `meta` (the only arguments in scope) is typed to
   carry source text — confirming D6's design point #1 ("nothing is typed to hold it") also means
   nothing carries it this far by construction, not merely by discipline.

5. **`run_validate`** (cli.py line 970, the bare `validate` CLI command's implementation) is
   confirmed by its own docstring and inline comment to never have source text at all: *"Re-check
   the existing curated tree, acquiring nothing (contract §1)"* and *"No source text is ever
   re-acquired here ... so this run has no evidence of digest drift."* It reads only the
   already-curated tree from disk (`read_curated_tree`). There is no code path by which a bare
   `validate` re-run could reach source text, now or with any change scoped to this feature —
   confirmed structural, not a gap to close.

## Offline fixture build check

Ran the existing offline fixture build over the committed `fixtures/minimal` set
(`rules-pipeline build --fixtures fixtures/minimal --offline --dry-run`, no live acquisition) to
confirm the trace against real control flow rather than reading it cold: the run executes the
`with workspace(root) as work:` block, populates `detail`, exits the block, and proceeds through
`check_snapshot`, `emit_bundle`, and `scan_bundle` to produce a report and bundle (it exits
non-zero on this deliberately undersized fixture set's own coverage-collapse findings, which is
expected and unrelated to this trace). No behaviour contradicted the static trace. `--dry-run`
regenerated two acquisition-id/timestamp fields in the committed fixture build's own output
files; those were reverted, and the run's own throwaway bundle/report output was deleted, so this
check left no lasting change.

## Consequence for later tasks (the answer T001 owes)

**Which stage should call the equivalence check instead**: the equivalence check (T052) must run
**inside `build`'s `with workspace(root) as work:` block**, alongside (not instead of) the
mechanic-digest computation it already scopes there — i.e., before `detail` goes out of scope,
using `detail`'s row text and the already-computed `render/loadout.py` output for the same
datasheet. It **cannot** be wired into `run_validate`'s call sites (cli.py line 1003-1009) or into
`check_snapshot` as invoked at line 805, because neither has source text available by the time it
runs.

This also means the equivalence check is **build-time only**, exactly as FR-019 already implies
and as the digest check already establishes precedent for: a bare `validate` re-run reports
whatever the previous `build` run recorded (or nothing, on a fixture/tree with no prior
equivalence figures) rather than re-deriving anything, the same way a bare `validate` re-run
already trusts a stored `review_state` as-is for the digest check with `ability_current_digests=
None`. T053's "wire into the `validate` stage's `run_validate`/`check_snapshot` call sites" should
be read as **wiring the check's stage identity and gating** (`WGC_EQUIVALENCE_CHECK_ENABLED`,
finding codes, coverage figures) into the same places those already land in the report — not as
literally invoking the comparison from either of those two functions, which is the one thing this
trace rules out.
